title: The Irbic cross
place: Churchyard of the monastery at Llandough

cast.G_DAI: a carter who hauls the stone (fictional)

shots.direction: Date-and-place card over an establishing wide shot. Grey spring morning on the inland hilltop at Llandough. A small early-medieval church of rough stone with a thatched roof stands inside a low earth-and-stone churchyard bank, with a few simple grave markers in the grass. Beyond the bank the land falls away to the Ely, its marshes, and the estuary as a pale far-off sheen. A freshly dug socket pit waits beside the church door. Slow push in.

lines.accent: South Wales Welsh (draft, for native review)
lines.cy: Gan bwyll, gan bwyll nawr! Wo 'na. Yr holl ffordd lan y rhiw gyda'r garreg 'ma, Frawd, ac mae'r ychen wedi ennill eu gwair.
lines.en: Steady, steady now! Whoa there. All the way up the hill with this stone, Brother, and the oxen have earned their hay.
lines.es: ¡Despacio, despacio ahora! So, so. Todo el camino loma arriba con esta piedra, hermano, y los bueyes se ganaron el pasto.

shots.direction: The monk pulls back the sacking and lays a heavy hand on the carved interlace of the shaft. He speaks to the carter.

lines.accent: South Wales Welsh (draft, for native review)
lines.cy: Duw a fendithio'u hamynedd nhw, a'th amynedd dithau. Mae'r seiri meini wedi gorffen eu naddu. Edrych ar y cwlwm, Dai: un llinyn, drosodd a thano, heb dorri byth.
lines.en: God bless their patience, and yours. The masons have finished their cutting. Look at the knotwork, Dai: one cord, over and under, never broken.
lines.es: Que Dios bendiga su paciencia, y la tuya también. Los canteros terminaron de tallar. Mirá el nudo, Dai: un solo cordón, por arriba y por abajo, sin cortarse nunca.

shots.direction: The raising. Ropes thrown over a timber sheerleg, the carter and two lay brothers haul, and the oxen take the strain while the cross rises upright and drops into its socket beside the church door. Packing stones are rammed in. Slow tilt up the shaft as it settles.

captions.text: The Irbic cross was carved and set up at Llandough in the 10th–11th century. The day of its raising is a recreation.

shots.direction: The cross stands. The carter wipes his scalp with his sleeve, looks up at the carving and asks the monk.

lines.accent: South Wales Welsh (draft, for native review)
lines.cy: A'r enw sy wedi'i dorri arni? Alla i ddim darllen llythyren, Frawd.
lines.en: And the name cut on it? I can't read a letter, Brother.
lines.es: ¿Y el nombre que tiene tallado? Yo no sé leer ni una letra, hermano. ¿Vos me lo leés?

shots.direction: The monk traces the carved letters on the shaft with his finger as he answers. The lettering stays soft and illegible to camera. The church door is open behind him.

lines.accent: South Wales Welsh (draft, for native review)
lines.cy: Irbic. Mae'r enw wedi'i dorri fan hyn yn y garreg, a fan hyn y bydd e'n aros, wrth ddrws yr eglwys, lle mae'n rhaid i bob enaid sy'n mynd i mewn i weddïo fynd heibio iddi.
lines.en: Irbic. The name is cut here in the stone, and here it stays, by the church door, where every soul going in to pray must pass it.
lines.es: Irbic. El nombre está tallado acá, en la piedra, y acá se queda, junto a la puerta de la iglesia, por donde tiene que pasar toda alma que entra a rezar.

shots.direction: The monk raises his right hand in blessing before the cross. The carter pulls off nothing (he is bareheaded), bows and makes the sign of the cross. The oxen stand behind.
